issue_context.title: Grid view details shows `_PythonDecoratedOperator` instead of `@task.python`
issue_context.body: ### Apache Airflow version main (development) ### What happened I ran a dag and navigated to the details drawer in the grid view. Saw this: ### What you think should happen instead The class name was descriptive enough, but it's not a class I had ever directly referenced. It would be easier for me to correlate this detail with my code if `@task` showed up somewhere in whatever is displayed. ### How to reproduce Run any dag with task decorators, view details about those task instances ### Operating System Mac OS 12.3.1 ### Versions of Apache Airflow Providers _No response_ ### Deployment Virtualenv installation ### Deployment details installed via `pip install ~/src/airflow` cloned at 34154803a ran via `airflow webserver` ### Anything else I'm under the impression that a new endpoint might be needed to expose friendlier operator descriptions. ### Are you willing to submit PR? - [ ] Yes I am willing to submit a PR! ### Code of Conduct - [X] I agree to follow this project's [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/apache/airflow/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md)
comments:
The cause of this in the UI is that we are using `get_tasks` on the REST API which doesn't directly pass the operator name. Only via `class_ref.class_name`.

This fix would be to update the get_tasks endpoint to send an `operator`

cc: @norm

This is issue I raised in Slack a while ago:
https://apache-airflow.slack.com/archives/CCPRP7943/p1644846308701199
Maybe we could override `task_type` for this. I did a quick search and it seems this is only used for UI presentation now (need to double check).
Would it not be easier to *add* the operator name to the API results?
Yeah, there's a few UI only things we could probably also get rid of at the same time. But I think `task.operator` would be easiest to understand for anyone using the API
Looking into this, and I'm not sure what we are looking for to replace `_PythonDecoratedOperator` if it is not the task's ID? If it is that, it is already in the API results.

It should not be the task_id. it should be the Operator class name..
`_PythonDecoratedOperator` should become `PythonOperator`

But `_PythonDecoratedOperator` _is_ the class name, which is the problem 🙂 It’s impossible to know exactly what class in the hierarchy chain the API should show (for example, we want `_PythonDecoratedOperator` to show its superclass `PythonOperator`, but we don’t want `PythonVirtualEnvOperator` to show `PythonOperator`). It’d be easier if we let the class implement what they want the API/UI to display for it.

True but we probably can distinguish.
Decorators also inherit from `DecoratedOperator`.

> It’d be easier if we let the class implement what they want the API/UI to display for it.

yeah maybe it's prefered. We can set in `BaseOperator` something like:

    def get_operator_ui_name_(self):
        return self.__class__.__name__
       
 and specific operators that need to change the name can override this method.

> Maybe we could override `task_type` for this. I did a quick search and it seems this is only used for UI presentation now (need to double check).

Task type is also used for metrics form DagRun creation:

```python
                Stats.incr(f"task_instance_created-{task_type}", count)
```

But I'd probably argue that the current value is as "wrong" there as it is in the UI.
Just heads up, this isn't just the API endpoint used by Grid view. Here is the same issue in Graph view:

review_comments: I don't think this is needed anymore, as operator_name is now a property, not a plain attribute?

I followed how `_task_type` is handled, which is why it was there. Now, if I take it out, `tests/serialization/test_dag_serialization.py::test_operator_expand_serde` fails. I'll have a further dig into it.
Oh, `_operator_name` is on MappedOperator, so rather than adding this here, add that in to the same named function in MappedOperator instead.
I'm not sure I understand your suggestion — `_operator_name` is the same trick as `_task_type` to preserve the name of *any* operator during serialisation. It is not specific to one?
(and tests fail if I move it as suggested, although that could be that the test is doing the wrong thing)

On my (admittedly somewhat cursory) reading of this code, a BaseOperator should never have an attribute called `_operator_name`, that only exists as a field on `MappedOperator` instances. Have I read it wrong?
